<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **10** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via resolvePredicateRelated (symbol, a method of class ObjectQL))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via cascadeDeleteRelations (symbol, a method of class ObjectQL))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **17** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 44639665eea4adc6de1eaa963ccd0e5a3e875f98` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e56561a4a05b18c2c3aa297170bd892d032dbf7e` — the merge of head `9a31fc9925e5a930aa5ae2a7c51b766a9883c448` into base `44639665eea4adc6de1eaa963ccd0e5a3e875f98`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e56561a4a05b18c2c3aa297170bd892d032dbf7e && git checkout e56561a4a05b18c2c3aa297170bd892d032dbf7e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 44639665eea4adc6de1eaa963ccd0e5a3e875f98 9a31fc9925e5a930aa5ae2a7c51b766a9883c448 && git checkout -B drift-repro 44639665eea4adc6de1eaa963ccd0e5a3e875f98 && git merge --no-ff 9a31fc9925e5a930aa5ae2a7c51b766a9883c448

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 44639665eea4adc6de1eaa963ccd0e5a3e875f98
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 44639665eea4adc6de1eaa963ccd0e5a3e875f98` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b1de69f917de0629e5d1c3789aad360e44ada51e`

Scope read:
- card #20006, body and 3 comments (the os-dev report is treated as a claim);
- #18682 records `5790469129` (round-11 Q1, options A–D verbatim), `5792704279` and `5795813514`;
- the PR body, and the whole diff `fc6ddb87a..b1de69f91` (5 files);
- AGENTS.md (Prime Directives, the runtime-strings rule) and `contract-review.md`;
- at head: `rule-validator.ts`, `engine.ts` (`resolvePredicateRelated`, `cascadeDeleteRelations`), `operation-private-keys.ts`, `ENTRY_EXECUTION_CONTEXT_FIELDS`, `field.zod.ts` `deleteBehavior`, and plugin-security's `delete-reference-cleanup-system-identity.test.ts`.

Run in the reviewer's own detached worktree at head, which was removed afterwards:
- the two pin files (63/63), the plugin-security fixture (18/18), and eslint over the 4 touched files (0/0);
- a probe of 14 delete shapes, 12 write shapes and 7 multi-value shapes, run at head AND with both source files reverted to the merge base;
- the built d.ts.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The refused set is unchanged: RIGHT.** Over the 14 delete shapes, base and head give identical verdicts, and `code` + `fields[]` (whole `constraint`) are byte-identical. `record.amount > 100 && record.account.status == 'closed'` (amount 50) and a `has(record.account.status)`-guarded rule pass the cleanup at base and at head. The 12 ordinary writes and 7 multi-value shapes are identical too. The refusal stays fail-closed.
- **Option D's literal mechanism is rejected: RIGHT.**
  - Option D (`5790469129`) reads: "hand an explicit unavailable binding … needs a new RelatedUnavailableReason member, which is a public type".
  - `resolveTraversalScope` refuses before evaluation on any absent binding, so D's literal mechanism would refuse the two shapes above, which is a narrowing. `RelatedUnavailableReason` is in the published d.ts.
  - The ruled direction, 「让外键清空的拒绝文字指对对象」, is implemented on the fault path instead.
- **The error envelope is unchanged: RIGHT.** `VALIDATION_FAILED`, `rule_violation`, `_record` and `constraint {rule, reason:'unevaluable', fault, missingKey}` are byte-identical in every refused shape. Only `message` differs, and only in the cleanup shapes.
- **The new text is reached only on the right write: RIGHT, with one corner (③ F1).**
  - The cause is read at one site, inside the pre-existing `__referentialFieldClear` branch, and handed only to the row matching `referencingId` on `referencingObject`.
  - These keep today's text (measured): an inherited context on another row, a hand-emptied reference, an own-column fault (`record.nope`), and ordinary writes.
- **SECURITY / disclosure: RIGHT, nothing new.**
  - The cleanup UPDATE runs under the deleter's own identity, exempt only from the object-level CRUD check. Only the pre-delete probe runs as system.
  - The new text names the parent object and id (the caller supplied both), the child object, the reference field, the rule name and the traversed column. Each was already disclosed by the old text, `constraint`, or the sibling restrict path (ruling #12166 c2, `err.dependentObject`). No count is disclosed.
  - The referencing row's id never reaches the text (measured).
  - A cleanup of a row the deleter cannot write is refused earlier with `PERMISSION_DENIED`. The #18682 secret/public equivalence pin is green.
  - The cause cannot be forged from REST: the entry context list is closed, with no `__` key, and forwarding consumers strip the `__` prefix. It authorizes nothing.
- **The prescriptions are true: RIGHT, with an undisclosed cost (③ F2).**
  - The guard makes the same delete succeed. An ordinary write with the reference set still refuses with the authored message.
  - `deleteBehavior` is `z.enum(['set_null','cascade','restrict'])` on `FieldSchema`. `cascade` deletes the child and `restrict` gives `DELETE_RESTRICTED` 409, measured on single- and multi-value references.
  - Offering only `deleteBehavior` for multi-value references is right: the cleanup keeps the other members, so the guard would still run the rule (measured: still refused).
- **Public surface: RIGHT.** The new names have 0 hits in the built `index.d.ts`, `core.d.ts` and util chunk (control: `RelatedRecordBinding` has 1/1/3). There is no new error code. `update()` and `OperationContext` are untouched. There is no tracker number in the runtime string.
- **Ablation: RIGHT.** Both files reverted to base give 7 red of 68: the 3 new-text pins and the 4 evaluator pins. The other #20006 pins measure existing behaviour and stay green.
- **CI at head:** 34 runs, 31 success, 3 skipped (`Console Pin Gate`, `Build Docs`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`), 0 failures. Every required context is `success`.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/objectql: patch` with `Clause-②: no` is correct. A runtime message changes, while the accept set is measured unchanged, the envelope is byte-identical, and no reachable type, option, export or error code moves.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Changeset:** every sentence is TRUE, including the example block, which equals the generated message at head, with ONE exception. Bullet 3, "**Unchanged:** a rule whose fault is in its own columns … keep today's text byte for byte", is **FALSE in a measured shape (F1)**.

**Shipped refusal text at head:** every sentence of the single-value and multi-value forms is TRUE. The guard sentence is true as a repair for the delete, but silent about its cost (F2).

**F1: attribution by key name misfires on a name collision.**
- The case: `record.status == 'x' && record.account.status == 'closed'` on a `crm_deal` that declares no `status`. CEL faults on the bare `record.status`, with the same fault at base.
- Head nevertheless emits the cleanup text, because a missing key that is ALSO read through a reference is attributed to the reference.
- The rule is broken on every write, not by the cleanup. So the changeset's "Unchanged" bullet and the PR body's "A fault on the rule's own columns keeps the generic text" are false for this shape.

**F2: the guard silently stops enforcing a rule that reads ANOTHER reference.**
- Following "Guard the rule on `account` being set" for `record.region.kind == 'secret'` makes that rule skip every `crm_deal` whose `account` is empty, on every insert and update.
- Measured: a guarded rule on an account-less deal with a secret region is accepted; unguarded, it is refused.
- The text says only "still judged on every write where the reference is set". An author following a prescription must be told what it costs (PD #10).

**PR body:** TRUE where measured, including the option-D argument, the untouched `OperationContext` / `update()`, the d.ts counts, eslint, plugin-security 18/18, the `__`-prefix stripping, and "row id never reaches the text". The failing-probe-first count and the per-ablation counts are UNMEASURED; the reviewer's full revert is consistent. The #20007 reuse note is TRUE: `referenceGuardRepair(field)` is module-local in the same file. #20007 should carry F2's cost clause where it applies.

**Out-of-scope finding: REAL.** Through `ExpressionEngine.evaluate`, all seven `ConditionalValidationSchema` TSDoc example predicates in `packages/spec/src/data/validation.zod.ts` fail when copied: six give `parse: Unexpected character: =`, and `order_total > 10000` gives `Unknown variable`. The strings ship in the spec d.ts.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-20006-cascade-fk-clear-refusal-text`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Bvd69VPa6puiNzzPUroDBx`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

What must change (small, and both in files the claim already owns):
1. **F1.** Choose one:
   - tighten the attribution, so that a missing key that is also read bare at the root (`record.KEY`) keeps the generic text, pinned with `record.status == 'x' && record.account.status == 'closed'` on an object declaring no `status`;
   - or narrow the changeset bullet and the PR body to what the code does.
2. **F2.** Where the rule reads a DIFFERENT reference, state the guard's cost in the text and in the changeset bullet "It applies whether…", e.g. "(the rule is then not judged on crm_deal records whose `account` is empty)". Or offer only `deleteBehavior` in that arm. Pin the account-less ordinary write in whichever direction the text promises.

Isolated reviewer: a contract-review-tier subagent, fed only the card, the #18682 records, the PR and AGENTS.md; adopted by the seat.
